patch_description:
The previous candidate (using a dedicated "theta_xx_long" parameter for the antipodal shell) regressed performance (0.55 vs 0.61 for the simpler 2-parameter design). The 2-parameter design (global RY + global RZ, all three CRZ shells sharing "theta_z") was the best-performing configuration so far, but it uses only Z-type generators for all entanglers, which may limit how well it can separate the hardest validation samples (Z-only entanglement is insensitive to certain X/Y-plane state features).

Instead of adding a brand-new parameter for long-range coupling (which hurt generalization) or reusing "theta_z" on the same wires with an X-type gate (which the seed's own analysis found kills the gradient by composing to a near-fixed net rotation), we replace only the long-range (distance-4, antipodal) shell's CRZ gates with CRX gates that reuse the existing "theta_ry" parameter. This is the natural entangling counterpart of the RY single-qubit layer (mirroring how CRZ is the natural counterpart of the RZ layer), injects a genuinely non-commuting (X-type) long-range correlation channel, and does so without adding any new trainable parameter (still 2 distinct circuit params, 4 total with gain/bias) and without the same-wire same-angle double-rotation degeneracy that broke trainability before (CRX(theta_ry) acts on different wires — the antipodal ring — than the CRZ(theta_z) short-range shells, and pairs with a genuinely different generator than the co-located RZ layer, avoiding accidental cancellation). This should improve robustness on hard validation groups while preserving the strong parameter economy of the best prior result.
